title: Reservation holds misbehave
prompt:
We've had a run of support tickets about stock reservations (the inventory package), and they all seem to come from ReservationService and the code under it:

1. Product pages show items as sold out long after shoppers abandon their carts. The stock only comes back after the nightly cleanup job (sweep_expired) has run.
2. A hold whose time is exactly up still blocks stock and can still be paid for in that same instant.
3. A support agent clicked "release" twice on a cart and afterwards we sold more lamps than we had: the availability went up by twice the cart.
4. Releasing a hold that was already paid for puts the units back on sale.
5. Some customers were charged for orders whose hold had already expired; checkout should have refused them. And a double click on "Pay" took the stock out of the ledger twice.
6. The mobile app retries reserve() with the same request_id after a timeout, and those customers end up with two holds for the same cart line.

The intended behaviour is written down in docs/reservations.md, and the checkout, the support tool and the app all rely on it: hold statuses (including "expired" being reported as soon as the time is up), how availability is computed, idempotent retries, and what release and confirm return or raise in each state. Please find and fix the causes so the service behaves as documented. Keep the public API (ReservationService, StockLedger, the clock classes and the exception types) as it is; the existing tests must still pass.
acceptance: Expired holds stop counting without a sweep and at exactly expires_at; get_hold reports expired; stock freed by expiry can be re-reserved; sweep_expired changes nothing observable and returns the count; double release returns False and cannot cause overselling; release after confirm raises HoldStateError; confirm after expiry raises HoldExpiredError without touching stock; double confirm is idempotent; confirm of released raises HoldStateError; retries with the same request_id return the same hold in any status, conflicting retries raise IdempotencyConflictError, failed reservations are not remembered; input validation; unknown ids raise HoldNotFoundError.
difficulty_rationale: Several interacting bugs across holds.py and service.py (a cached reservation counter that ignores expiry and double-counts, an off-by-one expiry boundary, missing state checks, an idempotency map keyed by the wrong id); patching symptoms one at a time leaves the counter and the sweep inconsistent.
